newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Bids show mining giants vie for ZCCM assets. [CORRECTED 16:15 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Bids show mining giants vie for ZCCM assets. [CORRECTED 16:15 GMT]

text.p: The world's largest mining companies are interested in acquiring some Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines (ZCCM) assets up for sale -- but not all -- bids opened in the Zambian capital on Friday showed.
Most bidders rejected packages designed by the Zambia Privatisation Agency and opted to bid for ZCCM assets under their own packages.
There were five bids for parts of the package "A" comprising the prized Nkana and Nchanga divisions which account for half ZCCM copper production.

ZPA said bidders for part of this package were -- a consortium comprising Avmin Ltd, Phelps Dodge Corp, Noranda Inc and the Commonwealth Development Corp; Metorex; Straits Resources; the Binani Group; and Sterlite Industries (India) Ltd (corrects by removing reference to Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd).
The Binani Group, Sterlite Industries, Straits Resources, Reunion Mining, AUR Resources and First Quantam Minerals bid for parts Luanshya Division.
AUR Resources, Sterlite Industries, and Farrell Financial Ltd bid for the Mufulira underground mine and concentrator, which in 1995-96 produced around 52,000 tonnes of copper in concentrate.

Four companies bid for the currently non-operational Chambishi copper mine: Sterlite Industries, Farrell Financial Ltd, First Quantam Minerals and AUR Resources. Chambishi has proven reserves of 33.5 million tonnes grading 2.55 percent copper.
There were no bidders for the Nampundwe pyrite mine, which in 1995-96 produced around 240,000 tonnes of ore.

The Binani Group, First Quantam Minerals, the Avmin consortium and another consortium of Camac International Ltd and ZCCM managers, and First Quantam bid for the Chambishi cobalt plant, which has a nominal capacity of 2,400 tonnes per year.
Fist Quantam Minerals were the only bidders for the Ndola precious metals plant, which produces gold, silver and selenium from copper refinery slimes.
There were three bids for the ZCCM power division, from Tractebel, Midlands Power International and Eskom.
Cyprus Amax and the Avmin consortium bid for Chingola refractory ores.
Opening the bids, Zambia Privatisation Agency chief Valentine Chitalu said no more bids would be accepted after February 28.
"Bids will be considered by our advisers, the ZCCM board, the ZPA board, and finally by the government. They will be finally approved by the cabinet," he said.
